title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
statement:
The values of the linked list `head` appear in non-decreasing order. Any value that occurs more than once must vanish completely: remove every node carrying it, not only the extra copies. Values that occur exactly once stay, in their original order.

Return the head of the remaining list, which is still sorted. If nothing remains, return an empty list.
constraints: The list is sorted in non-decreasing order
notes:
## Intuition

A brute-force idea counts how often each value occurs and rebuilds a list from the values seen once. Because the list is sorted, equal values sit next to each other in one block, so a single pass can spot a block of copies (a node whose successor has the same value) and unlink the whole block at once. A dummy node in front of `head` makes removing the first block no different from removing any other.

## Approach

1. Create `dummy` pointing at `head`. `prev` is the last node known to survive (initially `dummy`); `node` walks the list.
2. If `node.next` has the same value as `node`, this value is duplicated: remember it as `value` and advance `node` past every node holding it.
3. Link `prev.next` to the first node after the block. `prev` does not move, because that node has not been checked yet.
4. Otherwise `node` is unique: it becomes the new `prev`, and `node` steps forward.
5. Return `dummy.next`.

## Example 1, step by step

List `1 → 2 → 3 → 3 → 4 → 4 → 5`. Nodes `1` and `2` differ from their successors, so `prev` moves onto `2`. At the first `3` the next value is also `3`: `node` skips both and lands on the first `4`, and `2.next` now points there. That `4` also has a twin, so `node` skips to `5` and `2.next` becomes `5`. Node `5` has no successor, so it is kept. The result is `[1, 2, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is visited once, either kept or skipped.
- Space: O(1): only a few pointers and the dummy node.

## Pitfalls

- Removing only the extra copies (keeping one `3`) solves the easier problem 83, not this one.
- Do not advance `prev` after cutting a block; the next node may start another duplicated block.
- Without a dummy node, a duplicated first value (`[1, 1, 2]`) needs a separate case for the new head.
- Check `node !== null` before reading `node.val` when skipping a block that reaches the end.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dummy` | placeholder node in front of `head` |
| `prev` | last node known to stay in the answer |
| `node` | node currently being examined |
| `value` | the duplicated value being skipped |

narration.2: Put a dummy node in front of the list so the head can be removed like any other node.
narration.3: prev is the last node known to stay; at first that is the dummy.
narration.4: node walks through the original list.
narration.6: Process nodes until the end of the list.
narration.7: If the next node has the same value, this value is duplicated.
narration.9: Skip every node that carries it.
narration.12: Link the last kept node past the whole block of copies.
narration.14: The value is unique, so this node stays and becomes the new prev.
narration.15: Move on to the next node.
narration.18: The dummy's successor is the head of the cleaned list.
